threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stare in awe at brunch menus longer than an episode of EastEnders, trying to decipher what 'avocado toast' really means.
Last night on the 59, a guy debated whether to eat his cold kebab or save it for breakfast—total silence until he said, 'It's a hero, not a zero.'

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw the guy at the corner bakery bargaining with the cashier over a stale croissant, I knew I was truly embedded in Neukölln's vibe.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a nightclub in an old public bathhouse, complete with mosaics and a sauna. Party while surrounded by history!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their disdain for the overpriced tacos at that touristy spot on 24th—real ones know La Taqueria never disappoints.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy trying to fix his shattered phone screen with duct tape on the 38. Classic Tenderloin moment, and it somehow felt right.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but many locals avoid them on weekends—too crowded with selfie sticks.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their baffled look as they try to figure out the ‘no honking’ rule on Carrer de Verdi during brunch hours.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still avoid walking through London Fields after dark, clutching your keys like a dagger. The rest of us just stroll through without a second thought.
Last night on the 47, a guy serenaded the entire bus with his guitar, only to get off at the next stop and leave us all stunned.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I heard a neighbor yelling about the BVG strike while watering their plants. Only in Neukölln do we mix protest with gardening.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop run by a retired opera singer offering free concerts on Fridays. The blend of flavors and notes is unbeatable.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they know which taco trucks keep their meat fresh at the Sunday farmers' market—always the ones with the longest lines.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a woman in the Muni shelter meticulously folding hundreds of origami cranes while waiting for the 47. Total peace in the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals are drinking vermut at 1 PM. Most of us are just trying to catch the bus on time. It's not a party here, just life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion over La Rambla—staring at their map while walking in circles, missing the local side streets.
